findings.claim: `--compare-thinking` combined with `--native-citations` now sets `use_native_citations=args.native_citations` on the secondary pass while storing/labelling it as `faithfulness_thinking_on` / "thinking on"; the old code forced native off for pass B, so the A/B comparison silently varies two independent variables.

`_quality_value` is applied to every entry in `thresholds.metrics`, including skipped and unmeasured ones, so any future non-[0,1] threshold (latency, counts, token budgets) makes the gate a permanent exit 2 rather than a metric the checker ignores.

the new catch-all prints only `type(exc).__name__`, discarding the message; the actionable `ValueError` text from `_load_queries(args.negatives/args.extended/args.corpus_queries)` and from the `--min-precision`/`--min-faithfulness`/`--k` validators is lost, leaving CI with only `error: local_error:ValueError`.

moving the precision gate ahead of the negatives/extended/generalization passes means a retrieval regression now produces none of the advisory diagnostics that previously accompanied the failure, exactly when triage needs them.

the outcome validator hardcodes `"faithfulness_legacy" in report` for `completed`, so a `--compare-thinking` run (which writes `faithfulness_thinking_off`) would be rejected as invalid evidence; `extract_metrics` has the same single-key assumption.
`always() && rc != '0' && rc != '1'` also fires on job cancellation and whenever an earlier step fails and `check` is skipped (empty `rc`), attributing unrelated failures to "validation error".

RC precedence maps `BENCH_RC=2` plus `FAITH_RC=1` to `RC=1`, reporting a local/harness failure as a measured quality regression (covered and locked in by the `completed-faithfulness-before-error` case).
`math.isfinite(value)` is unreachable — `0 <= value <= 1` already rejects NaN and ±inf — so the ordering comment documents dead code.

`--calibrate --with-faithfulness` returns 0 while leaving `outcomes.faithfulness == "pending"`, i.e. a success exit paired with an unresolved outcome; only the workflow validator catches this, not the CLI.

`payload["calibration"] = cal` is not pre-checked with `json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False)` the way `negatives` is, so one non-finite calibration value fails the entire receipt write instead of that section.

`_save_progress` now serialises and rewrites the dump up to three times per run and prints "Wrote per-query JSON" to stderr each time; the final write in `main` duplicates the checkpoint written by `_run_faithfulness_passes`.

the generator variable `path` in the `expected_in_top_3` check shadows the `_load_queries` parameter of the same name used two lines above in the error message; correct by genexp scoping but easy to misread and to break in a later edit.

the `bad-options` case assumes a bare `--compare-thinking` is rejected, but the only guard visible in the diff is `if args.compare_thinking and args.thinking`; confirm an explicit "requires --with-faithfulness" check exists or the case asserts the wrong exit path.

`_dump()` pins the real `tests/golden/queries.yaml` and repo `thresholds.json`, so every workflow-replay case fails during any PR that legitimately re-measures the baseline sha, and the 20s subprocess timeout at line 113 is tight given each case spawns four-plus real interpreters.
